summary: This `auth.js` module sets up an Express router dedicated to user authentication. It imports `bcrypt` for hashing passwords, `jsonwebtoken` for issuing access tokens, and a custom `validateUser` helper function. The file outlines two POST route handlers: `/register` for new user creation and `/login` for user authentication. Finally, it exports the router to be integrated into the main Express application, forming the foundational routing logic for secure user sign-up and login workflows.

The `new_file.txt` file is a simple text document containing the single string "this is my new file". It serves as a basic placeholder, initialization file, or test artifact within the repository, designed to verify file creation, text storage, and reading capabilities in the project.

This `package.json` configures `taskflow-api` (v1.0.0), a Node.js task management API featuring JWT authentication, created by the TaskFlow Team under the MIT license. It sets `server.js` as the application entry point. Execution scripts are provided for production (`npm start`) and local development (`npm run dev`). Runtime dependencies include Express for API routing, JsonWebToken and Bcrypt for secure authentication and password hashing, and Dotenv for managing environment variables. Nodemon is included as a dev dependency to enable dynamic server reloads during development.

The `product.txt` file serves as a simple descriptive document establishing the initial identity of the project. Its content declares that this repository represents the developer's first product release, acting as a foundational, high-level descriptor within the codebase.

This `server.js` file serves as the main entry point and setup script for the TaskFlow Express.js REST API. It initializes the Express application, configures global middleware to parse incoming JSON requests, and sets up environment-based port configuration defaulting to 3000. 

The file mounts modular routing logic for authentication (`/api/auth`) and task management (`/api/tasks`). It also exposes a `/health` endpoint that returns server health status and a current timestamp. Finally, it starts the HTTP server on the specified port and exports the configured application instance for testing or external invocation.
